name: Omi
description: Omi is a Sri Lankan partnership plain-trick game of the Whist type. Four players in fixed partnerships bid trumps after seeing only their first four cards, then receive four more. Play is counter-clockwise. The 20 unused cards (2-6) serve as scoring tokens; the first team to collect 10 tokens wins.

overview.description: Omi is a Sri Lankan partnership plain-trick game of the Whist type. Four players in fixed partnerships bid trumps after seeing only their first four cards, then receive four more. Play is counter-clockwise. The 20 unused cards (2-6) serve as scoring tokens; the first team to collect 10 tokens wins.

history.origins: Omi is a popular card game in Sri Lanka; in some regions it is known as Oombi. The name suggests a distant connection with Hombre, but little trace of that influence remains.
timeline: Unknown origins; likely colonial-era introduction or local development.
Present: Widely played across Sri Lanka as a social and family game.
history.cultural: A staple of Sri Lankan card play, often played in homes and social gatherings.
history.evolution: A straightforward partnership plain-trick game similar to Court Piece (Rang) in that the first player chooses trumps on the basis of only the first few cards.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships; partners sit opposite (North-South vs East-West).
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack; only 32 cards used (A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7). Rank A high to 7 low.
setup.dealing: Dealer shuffles and offers cut to opponent on left. Dealer deals 4 cards to each player. Player to dealer's right announces trump (without consulting partner). Dealer then deals 4 more cards to each (8 total).
setup.equipment: 32 playing cards; 20 token cards (2-6 of each suit). One player holds black tokens (clubs, spades 2-6); an opponent holds red tokens (hearts, diamonds 2-6).

rules.objective: Take more tricks than the opponents. Teams score token cards; first team to collect 10 or more tokens wins.
rules.gameplay: 1. After trump is announced, player to dealer's right leads any card. 2. Play proceeds counter-clockwise. Players must follow suit if able; otherwise may play any card. 3. Highest trump wins; if no trump played, highest card of suit led wins. 4. Trick winner gathers cards, leads next trick. 5. After 8 tricks, tokens are awarded according to the scoring table.
keyRules: Trump chosen by player to dealer's right after seeing only first 4 cards.
Token scoring: 4-4 split = no tokens, but extra token next time a team takes more than 4.
5-7 tricks for trump-choosing team = 1 token; for non-declarers = 2 tokens.

strategy.basic: When choosing trumps, select the suit in which you have most cards. Between two equal suits, prefer the one without the aceâ€”the ace is likely to win a trick whether trump or not.
strategy.intermediate: Remember what cards have been played. Do not normally beat or trump your partner's winning card. Use discards to signal: if partner leads and you have no cards of that suit, discard from a suit you want led (e.g. your highest or only card of that suit).
strategy.advanced: Finesse: holding ace and queen of a led suit, play the queen to gain a trick when the opponent to your left has the king. With four cards in four different suits, picking trump is a guess; some players choose the suit of the lowest card.
tips: When holding four cards in three suits with two low in one suit, some choose the suit you have none of, hoping partner gets trumps.

variations.name: Announced Kapothi
variations.description: To win 3 tokens for taking all 8 tricks, you must announce before the seventh trick that you intend to win all eight. If you then lose one of the last two tricks, you give 4 tokens to the opponents.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Announced Kapothi changes only the penalty for failing the bid; no engine constant overrides documented yet.

scoring.description: Token cards (2-6 of each suit) are used as scoring chips. Black and red tokens are kept separate.
scoring.winCondition: First team to win 10 or more tokens. A team loses when they run out of tokens to pay.

synthesis.shortDescription: Sri Lankan 4-player partnership trick game. Trump chosen after first 4 cards. First team to 10 tokens wins.
